sahneler.metin: A dam is one wall holding back an entire lake.
The water pushes on it every second, day and night.
The quiet killer is water that seeps THROUGH the dam.
It slowly carries away soil, carving a hidden tunnel inside.
Engineers call this piping, and you cannot see it happening.
If water ever pours over the top, it erodes the dam in minutes.
Once a small breach opens, the pressure rips it wide open.
A wall of water then races downstream faster than a car.
That is why dams are watched with sensors around the clock.
